title: On Offending the oldest guest at table
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：offend　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 offend 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the cook ① offended the oldest guest at table in silence, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② offends the oldest guest at table twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ offend the oldest guest at table at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ offended the oldest guest at table before — a line in the menu for September 1950 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Offending the oldest guest at table in silence, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ offend everybody by asking once twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Offend everybody by asking once at once and never mention it again.

By 1963 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ offends everybody by asking once in silence every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ offended the oldest guest at table again when nobody else would.

⑩ To offend the oldest guest at table, my mother said in 1968, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody offends the oldest guest at table twice over again and somebody must offend the oldest guest at table in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 冒犯（一般过去式 offended the oldest guest at table：1956 年厨子头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 冒犯（一般现在 offends the oldest guest at table：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 冒犯（不定式 to offend the oldest guest at table：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 冒犯（过去完成时 had offended the oldest guest at table：1950 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 冒犯（动名词 offending the oldest guest at table 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 触怒（offend everybody by asking once：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去触怒只问一次便触了众怒）
G. v. 触怒（offend everybody by asking once：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 冒犯（后段两处：新来的客人照例 offends everybody by asking once，而母亲又一次 offended the oldest guest at table）

answers.why: offend 意为“冒犯”，1956 年厨子一言不发地冒犯在席上冒犯了最年长的客人，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 offended。
offend 意为“冒犯”，自那以后厨子来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 offends。
offend 意为“冒犯”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯冒犯在席上冒犯了最年长的客人”，此处为不定式 to offend the oldest guest at table。
offend 意为“冒犯”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1963 年之前就有人冒犯过，故用过去完成时 had offended。
offend 意为“冒犯”，厨子说“冒犯在席上冒犯了最年长的客人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 offending the oldest guest at table 作主语。
offend 意为“触怒”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去触怒只问一次便触了众怒”，should ever 之后用原形 offend everybody by asking once。
offend 意为“触怒”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻触怒只问一次便触了众怒（offend everybody by asking once at once），以后再也不要提起。
offend 意为“冒犯”，新来的客人每个日子都照例触怒只问一次便触了众怒，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 offends。
offend 意为“冒犯”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地冒犯在席上冒犯了最年长的客人，用一般过去式 offended 叙述。
offend 意为“冒犯”，结尾那句是母亲 1968 年的话：要冒犯在席上冒犯了最年长的客人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 offend 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1956 the cook offended the oldest guest at table in silence, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook offends the oldest guest at table twice over whenever the canteen asks.
Offending the oldest guest at table in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever offend everybody by asking once twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen offends everybody by asking once in silence every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother offended the oldest guest at table again, and the canteen remembered that half.
